description:
We’re sleep-deprived humans who looked at space, saw an absurd amount of data, and thought, “Yeah, we can probably figure this out.” Armed with questionable ideas, questionable code, and way too much caffeine, we’re turning NASA data into something that actually works. 

Mission: questionable; Code: compiling; Brain: offline; Space: yes
summary:
The project is based on the 'Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map'. 
Astronauts on Mars need a way to survive the windy and rocky nature of the planet. They must analyse the terrain and find the shortest route, hopefully the safest route, to their destinations. Our app provides 2D and 3D renders of the Martian terrain, showing statistics about the elevation, climate, and mineral composition of any set of coordinates chosen. The pathfinding tool allows the user to find the best path suited to requirements like fuel efficiency, safety, speed, and scientific interest.
details:
We used MOLA (Mars Orbital Laser Altimeter) data from NASA's MGS (Mars Global Surveyor) spacecraft to create a 2D render of the Martian heightmap. Climate data, Lightmap data, Mineral composition data, and more (from the same source) can be layered over this 2D map to give a topographical and geological understanding of the planet. This data can also be seen in a numerical format via our app. Our pathfinding uses these datasets to calculate the optimal path between two points, keeping in mind safety (least slope gradient), distance (time taken per travel), fuel efficiency (a necessary bias) and scientific interest (most diverse mineral composition). The importance of each bias stated above is manually editable in the pathfinding UI. Furthermore, a 3D globe view of Mars uses a special version of the pathfinding tool. The app can also provide 3D topography renders between any set of coordinates the user specifies, with custom exaggeration to scale the elevations up or view them 1:1. 

The app was primarily coded in Python. The UI was made using Flutter. The 2D and 3D renders use HTML, CSS and WebGL.

We openly acknowledge using Claude and Gemini to proofread our code and make it more efficient. We also acknowledge using Claude for troubleshooting and bug-fixing the code.

To our knowledge, this is the first app that unifies Martian geographical data with navigation on Mars, not only rendering a map, but adding features associated with navigation apps like Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps, etc. It is a simple, intuitive app available to all that collates open-source Martian data needed to survive there. We have considered factors like the least harsh slope, fuel efficiency, and one-route-most-minerals for the navigation tool. However, we have also noted that our app requires live syncing with artificial satellites on Mars to stream data efficiently and to record live weather, allowing us to train our tool to find a path around storms. Thus, our app aids, or can aid in the future, a manned exploration of Mars.
